text:
priya: Heads up — psionic13b-int4 canary is hitting OOMs on a subset of requests on dedicated nodes. Seen during long generative sessions (~>800 tokens) after a 2h warmup. Logs show repeated 'alloc fail' from tiling allocator and high slab fragmentation. Anyone seen this pattern with our memory_tiling + prefetch bias config?
kevin: ugh. yes, looks like fragmentation from aggressive prefetching + int4 KV layout. what are current defaults for this model? max_new_tokens / batch config?
priya: default model config on canary: `{"max_new_tokens": 1024, "batching.max_concurrent": 8, "prefetch_window": 64, "memory_tiling.enabled": true, "memory_tiling.prefetch_bias": 0.9}`. Canary runs at 1:1 traffic, repro rate ~ 6%.
maya: 0.9 is pretty aggressive. prefetch_bias that high will pull many KV chunks into hot memory and increase slab churn. lower it to 0.5 for int4 to reduce simultaneous slot grabs. also lower `batching.max_concurrent` to 2 for initial rollout.
sam: agree. also set `kv_trim_threshold` to 0.6 and enable soft-evict so we can keep latency but reclaim under pressure. Something like: `{"memory_tiling": {"prefetch_bias": 0.5, "soft_evict": true, "kv_trim_threshold": 0.6}}`
priya: thanks. quick question on max_new_tokens — should we drop default to 256 for this variant? Many of these OOM traces are with user prompts that then ask for long continuations.
kevin: for canary int4 I'd push conservative defaults: `max_new_tokens=256` and `client_max=1024` enforced via route-level limits if necessary. Reduces worst-case KV growth. Also turn on per-request kv_eviction="on-epoch" (our lightweight strategy) so very long requests don't accumulate forever.
priya: deployed a small patch with prefetch_bias=0.5 and max_new_tokens=256 on two canary hosts. Will monitor. Pushing `batching.max_concurrent=2` too.
infra-bot: deploy 6181819001 by priya to eng-dedicated-canary at 2024-11-05T15:12:24Z — success
maya: also run a short eval to check quality regressions before rolling out: compare Rouge/L score on our long-form summarization set (100 samples) with quantized int4 vs baseline int8. If quality delta > 1.5% we revisit.
sam: FYI, I ran a quick smoke earlier — int4 at prefetch_bias=0.9 had identical latency P50 but P95 spiked ~200ms and memory churn. With 0.5 bias P95 dropped ~120ms and fragmentation traces look much cleaner.
priya: good signal. starting a 24h canary and a small eval job. I'll post results. If OOM stops and quality delta < 1%, we roll to 10% traffic.
kevin: one more: add `slot_reserve: 0.08` to policy so we keep minimal free headroom for hot allocations. saved us before.
priya: added slot_reserve 0.08 in canary config. thanks. will update thread with metrics in ~2h. :thumbsup:
